claim_boundary.supports: Over an arbitrary type X (Lean, general; the cardinality statement frontier_card is informative only for finite X, frontierEquiv and minimalSelecting_iff_singleton carry the general content): no point is fixed by every permutation when X has two distinct points (the bare-set form of "no Sym(X)-equivariant distinguished-point selection"); a point is invariant under the pointwise stabiliser of a declared set S iff it lies in S or the complement of S is that single point; S selects some point iff S is nonempty or X has exactly one point; for X with two distinct points the inclusion-minimal selecting sets are exactly the singletons, one per point (a consequence of the pointwise-stabiliser definition: a declared point is fixed because it is declared); on a one-point carrier the empty declaration already selects and on an empty carrier nothing does. Replay bound (not part of the Lean claim): exact tables for every subset of every carrier of size 0..6 (127 subsets), invariant points by enumerating all permutations fixing S, and the minimal selecting sets.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Retention, dynamics or observers being impossible or available (WDP-CH03-N01 is a nonclaim, not formalised); that Selecting / MinimalSelecting formalises WDP-CH03-D01 (D01 minimises declared input sets whose removal restores a symmetry that moves the output, relative to an implementation class and dependency preorder; here the minimal declarations making some point invariant under the pointwise stabiliser are computed, and the two agree on singletons only because the output is the declared point); a Lean notion of equivariant selection function (no_fully_invariant_point is its bare-set specialisation); the price of selection on structured carriers (rigid, cyclic, graph) or under the setwise stabiliser; WDP-CH03-P03; infinite-carrier cardinality; any physical or interpretive claim.
